newsitem.title: JAPAN: ICO to buy dual mode phones from NEC and M'bishi.
newsitem.headline: ICO to buy dual mode phones from NEC and M'bishi.

text.p: Britain's ICO Global Communications (ICO) said on Monday it had signed contracts with NEC Corp and Mitsubishi Electric Corp to supply mobile phones with an integrated satellite aerial.

The contracts are part of ICO's commercial strategy to enlist multiple suppliers to bring to market around three million next-generation hand-held mode terminals, specially designed for ICO, over a three-year period starting in 2000, the company said.
An ICO spokesman did not provide the value of the contracts.

ICO was set up by 47 investors worldwide in 1994 to develop the International Mobile Satellite Organisation's (Inmarsat) satellite-based mobile telephone system. Inmarsat is a multinational cooperative based in London.

The ICO terminals, to be sold worldwide, will be pocket-sized and similar in design to current digital mobile phones. Retail prices are also expected to be at the same level as current mobile phones, ICO said.

ICO said the new phones will be dual-mode, able to work both on any cellular network and on ICO's satellite network. If no cellular network is available, the terminal will automatically switch to ICO's satellite network, it added.
Current mobile phones work on the cellular system, which allows communication through ground-based stations.
The satellite network offers communication services to mobile phone users at any time, almost anywhere in the world, ICO said.
ICO said the company expects to begin full operation in 2000.
